global.explanation: Gives one party unchecked, unilateral power with no objective standard.
Obligation never expires — unusually harsh outside confidentiality clauses.
Cannot be undone or renegotiated later, even if circumstances change.
Removes the other party's ability to prepare or react.
Signals the clause overrides normal fault/cause limitations.
Overly broad language often used to maximize scope of obligation.
One party is giving up a legal right — check what right is being waived and why.
Removes financial recourse even if the other party fails to perform.
No cap on exposure — a major deviation from standard risk allocation.
Explicitly excuses a party from a duty a reasonable counterpart would expect.
Lifetime obligation with no expiry — rarely enforceable and highly unusual.
Unilateral change of terms without counterparty protection.

Indemnification.explanation: Forces indemnification even for the indemnified party's own negligence — highly unusual and one-sided.
Removes any fault requirement, turning indemnity into unconditional insurance.

Limitation of Liability.pattern: no limitation or cap of any kind
Limitation of Liability.explanation: One party has zero liability protection — highly asymmetric.
Liability protection isn't fixed in the contract — it can be revoked unilaterally.

Termination.explanation: Client pays in full even if terminated early or for cause — unusually punitive.
Locks one party into a long-term obligation with no exit.

Confidentiality.pattern: for the rest of employee's life
Confidentiality.explanation: Perpetual personal obligation surviving employment — often unenforceable and a red flag.
Overreaches into ordinary professional knowledge, not just proprietary secrets.

Payment Terms.explanation: Pricing can change without negotiation or consent.
No refund even for total non-performance by the other party.

Intellectual Property.explanation: IP assignment reaches beyond the scope of the actual engagement.

Intellectual Property.pattern: on contractor's own time using contractor's own equipment
Intellectual Property.explanation: Claims ownership of work with no real connection to the engagement — legally aggressive.

Non-Compete.explanation: Geographic scope is almost certainly unenforceable and disproportionate.
Duration far exceeds typical enforceable non-compete windows.

Dispute Resolution.pattern: waives any right to a jury trial or class action
Dispute Resolution.explanation: Removes significant legal remedies available to the weaker party.

Force Majeure.explanation: One-sided force majeure that protects only one party.

Warranty.explanation: Disclaims all warranties — shifts quality risk entirely to the other party.

Warranty.pattern: no warranties of any kind whatsoever
Warranty.explanation: Total warranty disclaimer, unusually broad even for software.

Assignment.explanation: Contract obligations could be transferred to an unknown third party without consent.

Data Protection.pattern: sell, and share any personal data
Data Protection.explanation: Grants broad commercial rights over personal data with no restriction — likely non-compliant with data protection law.
